body.x: Solive Ventures, led by CEO Seo Ju-ho, participated in the ‘CES Unveiled’ global media event on January 7th, before the official opening of CES 2024 in Las Vegas. Originating as a student startup team from Seoul National University, Solive Ventures has developed intelligent solutions for children’s developmental home care. The three student entrepreneurs, Seo Ju-ho, Kwon Ik-hyun, and Choi Sung-hyun, who started in a Seoul National University College of Engineering club and participated in the Creative Design Festival at their university, established the company. In 2023, they were selected for the Preliminary Startup Package in the Social Venture category and attracted seed investment from Seoul National University Holdings in November of the same year.

At CES 2024, Solive Ventures exhibited ‘Peel & Play,’ an educational sensory toy to aid children’s brain development. They received innovation awards in the Accessibility & Aging Tech and Digital Health categories.

Peel & Play is a toy inspired by a simple orange, where children use the toy’s peel segments for various educational games. Attaching and detaching these unique pieces to and from the spherical body provides visual, tactile, and auditory feedback, enhancing children’s concentration, memory, and problem-solving abilities.
As Solive Ventures showcased Peel & Play at CES Unveiled, the global media event preceding CES, they received many positive responses from international journalists and influencers.

body.cap: Seo Ju-ho, CEO of Solive Ventures, interacting with international media at CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: CEO Seo Ju-ho stated, “Having been recognized with awards in two categories for Peel & Play, we aimed to have our product’s technical capabilities evaluated by global media experts in related fields. We are delighted with the favorable responses, especially from those hailing from countries and regions that highly emphasize children’s education and development, which also bodes well for our future competitiveness in the market.”

He added, “CES is an annual exhibition where technology companies worldwide gather to offer many sights. Amidst the vast and diverse exhibition space, we hope our booth provides visitors a moment of respite.”

The Consumer Technology Association (CTA), host of CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition, provides a platform in Las Vegas each January to showcase global consumer electronics trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been reporting CES news worldwide since 2006, highlighting products, companies, and technologies with the ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ awards programs. They also discuss issues in the field from the CES scene through ‘AVING LIVE.’

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion, operating on its most enormous scale since Seoul’s first CES participation in 2020, is a joint effort of 13 organizations, including SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Campus Town, AI Yangjae Hub, Gwanak District, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, Konkuk University, and Kyung Hee University. This collaborative pavilion marks a significant step in Seoul’s ambition to become a startup hub, and among its participating companies, 17 received innovation awards, evidencing their excellence. The pavilion also includes 85 supporters in a significant collaboration between companies, institutions, and industry-academia cooperation.
